Critics argue that a politician's silence on social media during solemn national anniversaries signals a lack of patriotism or evasion.

- Fox News Disclosure: COND (-0.6, -0.7) — Resurfaces old clips to stoke culture wars.
On the 25th anniversary of 9/11, conservative media scrutinized Texas politician James Talarico for posting about policy instead of memorializing the day on X, alongside resurfaced past remarks.

The Poison:
Transforming solemn national days of remembrance into routine partisan cudgels cheapens public discourse and exploits national trauma.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing a politician's personal social media feed choices with an absence of remembrance constitutes a Metaphysical plane error.

Social Physics Analysis:
Outlets deploy a Smart Selfish Maneuver, manufacturing an outrage crisis over social media silence to distract from substantive policy debates and score partisan points.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil through manufactured outrage loops.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public figures face intense scrutiny over every digital footprint during national anniversaries.

The Unavoidable Lie: Selective social media observation proves a total absence of civic grief.

Alethekanon:
Partisan media weaponizes digital omissions to manufacture artificial outrage cycles.

Awwthekanon:
When we turn days of deep national mourning into political weapons, we forget how to comfort one another in our shared grief.

Brothekanon:
Classic internet outrage factory mode: digging up old clips and counting tweets on a solemn anniversary just for clicks.

Spirithekanon:
"Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt" Colossians 4:6 PASS
Turning solemn national remembrance into partisan ammunition honors neither the dead nor the living.
